sections.heading: 1. Purpose and acceptance
paragraphs: These Terms of Service ("ToS") govern access to and use of the ZeroAPI service (the "Service"), operated by ZeroAPI SAS, a simplified joint-stock company incorporated under Senegalese law, registered in Dakar, with its registered office in Dakar, Senegal (hereinafter "ZeroAPI", "we").
Using the Service constitutes full and unreserved acceptance of these ToS. If you do not agree, you must not use the Service.

sections.heading: 2. Service description
sections.intro: ZeroAPI is an asynchronous backend generation platform. From a natural-language description, the Service produces:
items: a technical specification (models, endpoints, relationships);
TypeScript source code based on Hono.js;
automated tests (Vitest) and OpenAPI 3.1 documentation;
deployment options (Railway, Render, Vercel, Fly.io) or hosting on ZeroAPI infrastructure depending on the subscribed plan.
sections.outro: The Service is continuously evolving. Certain features may be marked "beta" and provided without warranty.

sections.heading: 3. User account

You must be at least 16 years old to use ZeroAPI. Professional accounts bind the represented organisation.

sections.outro: Payments are processed by Stripe. Mobile Money payment (Orange Money, Wave, MTN MoMo, Moov Money) is being integrated. cookies.title: Cookie
cookies.callout: You can refuse all non-essential cookies without degrading the site's functionality. No disguised consent wall: a "Reject" button is just as visible as the "Accept" button.

sections.heading: 1. What is a cookie?
sections.body: A cookie is a small text file placed by a website on your device (computer, mobile) via your browser. It may contain information such as a session identifier, a display preference, or a statistics counter. ZeroAPI also uses similar technologies (localStorage, sessionStorage) — they are covered by this policy.

sub.heading: 2.1 Strictly necessary cookies
sub.intro: These cookies are essential to the operation of the site. They do not require your consent.

rows.name: zeroapi-cookie-consent
rows.purpose: Remembers your choice on the cookie banner (localStorage)

sub.heading: 2.2 Analytics cookies (consent required)
sub.intro: If you accept, we use a privacy-respecting analytics tool (Plausible Analytics, self-hosted in Europe). No personal data is collected: no full IP address, no fingerprint, no cross-site cookie. Plausible uses an anonymous session identifier (hashed per day and per site) to distinguish visitors.

rows.name: _pl_*
rows.purpose: Anonymous audience measurement (page views, country, referrer)

sub.heading: 2.3 Third-party cookies
sub.intro: If you use Google or GitHub OAuth authentication, those services may place their own cookies on their respective domains. They are not accessible by ZeroAPI. Consult their policies:

sub.heading: 3.1 Consent banner
sub.intro: On your first visit, a banner invites you to accept or refuse non-essential cookies. Your choice is remembered for 6 months. You may change your mind at any time by:
items: deleting the zeroapi-cookie-consent key from your browser's localStorage, or
writing to dpo@zeroapi.app who will take care of it.

sub.heading: 3.2 Disabling cookies in your browser
sub.intro: You can configure your browser to block or delete cookies. Strictly necessary cookies are essential to the application's operation: blocking them will prevent you from logging in.

sections.heading: 4. No advertising tracking
sections.body: ZeroAPI does not display advertising, does not integrate with any advertising network, and does not share any cookie for marketing profiling purposes. No Facebook Pixel, no Google Ads, no retargeting.

sections.heading: 5. Updates
sections.body: This policy may be updated to reflect our practices and regulations. The date at the top of the page indicates the last update. In the event of a significant change, we will inform you by email or via a new consent banner.

meta.title: Security — ZeroAPI
meta.description: ZeroAPI's security architecture: encryption, authentication, secure generated code, responsible disclosure.

security.callout: We take security seriously because we generate code that will go into production. Here is how we protect your platform, your data, and the code we produce for you.

items.label: In transit
items.body: all communications use TLS 1.3 (TLS 1.2 minimum for backwards compatibility). HSTS enabled, automatic HTTPS redirect.

items.label: At rest
items.body: databases and object storage encrypted with AES-256. Backups are encrypted too.

items.label: Secrets
items.body: environment variables encrypted, quarterly rotation of sensitive keys, strict separation of environments (dev, staging, prod).

sections.heading: 2. Authentication and access
items: Passwords hashed with argon2id, never stored in plaintext.
OAuth 2.0 with Google and GitHub (the password is never transmitted to ZeroAPI).
Two-factor authentication (2FA) via TOTP (apps such as Authy, Google Authenticator) available for all accounts, mandatory for Business plans.
Short-lived sessions on the UI side, rotating refresh tokens on the API side.
SSO SAML / OIDC available on the Business plan for organisations.
Staff access: principle of least privilege, mandatory MFA, audit log of all admin actions.

sections.heading: 3. Security of generated code
sections.intro: Every backend generated by ZeroAPI includes by default:
items: Zod validation on all inputs (body, params, query, headers);
Contextual anti-XSS escaping and parameterised anti-SQLi queries (Prisma);
HTTP security headers (Helmet): CSP, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy;
Strict CORS configured explicitly, no wildcard unless requested;
Rate limiting per IP and per token, configurable per endpoint;
JWT authentication signed with HS256 or RS256, short expiry and key rotation;
Fine-grained RBAC by role and resource;
Structured logging with automatic masking of sensitive fields (passwords, tokens, card numbers).
sections.outro: A static security review (AST analysis + proprietary rules) is run before code delivery, and any critical alert blocks generation.

sections.heading: 4. Infrastructure
items: Hosted on AWS (regions eu-west-3, eu-central-1) and OVH (Roubaix, Strasbourg). Africa region (Dakar) being deployed.
Cloudflare at the front: DDoS protection, WAF, bot mitigation.
Encrypted backups every 6 hours, retained for 30 days, restoration tested monthly.
Multi-AZ architecture, automatic replication of critical data.

sections.heading: 5. Customer secrets lifecycle
sections.intro: The secrets you provide for deployment (Stripe API keys, cloud tokens, database credentials) are:
items: encrypted client-side with a PBKDF2-derived key before transit;
stored in a dedicated vault (Vault), never in plaintext in the database;
injected as environment variables only at the moment of deployment;
deleted from the vault 24 h after successful deployment.

sections.heading: 6. Incident management
sections.intro: Our on-call team is reachable 24/7 for Business plans. In the event of an incident affecting your data:
items: Notification by email and on status.zeroapi.app within 4 hours.
Notification to CDP (Senegal) and CNIL (France) within 72 hours in the event of a personal data breach, in accordance with GDPR Article 33.
Public post-mortem report published within 14 days after resolution.

sections.heading: 7. Responsible disclosure programme
sections.intro: Found a vulnerability? Thank you. Write to
items: a description of the issue and steps to reproduce it;
the estimated impact;
your contact details if you wish to be credited.
sections.response: We acknowledge receipt within 48 business hours. For confirmed vulnerabilities, we offer rewards ("bug bounty") based on severity, from €50 to €2,000. Any discovery made in good faith and within scope will not result in any legal action.
sections.outOfScope: Out of scope: denial of service, social engineering, physical attacks, already-reported vulnerabilities, testing on other users' accounts without their consent.

sections.heading: 8. Compliance and audits
items: GDPR compliance and Senegalese law no. 2008-12 — see our GDPR page.
ISO 27001 certification in progress (target Q4 2026).
Annual external penetration tests; summary reports available on request for Business customers.
Mandatory two-person code review for any change touching authentication, storage, payment, or generation.

sections.heading: 9. Your role
sections.intro: Security is a team effort. A few recommendations:
items: enable 2FA, use a password manager;
do not put real secrets in your prompts (use placeholders);
review the generated code before deploying to production;
keep your project dependencies up to date — we include Dependabot by default in the generated repo.

gettingStarted.title: Your
gettingStarted.subtitle: No local installation required. A browser and the desire to write a sentence is all you need.

callout.label: No credit card required.
callout.body: The free plan allows 3 generations per month and full Git export.

sections.heading: 1. Create an account
sections.intro: Go to app.zeroapi.app/register. Three sign-up options:
items: Email + password (verification by magic link);
Google OAuth;
GitHub OAuth.
sections.outro: Your default workspace is created automatically. You can invite other members later from

sections.heading: 2. Describe your API
sections.intro: In the dashboard, click New generation. You land on the prompt editor. A few useful rules:
items: Write in French, English, or Pidgin — ZeroAPI understands all three.
List the entities, their relationships, then the business rules.
Specify constraints: auth, roles, payments, notifications, files.

sections.heading: 3. Inspect the generated code
sections.intro: Generation is asynchronous — you can close the tab and we will notify you by email. Allow about two minutes for a medium-sized project. When it's ready, you access a file explorer with:
items: The complete Prisma schema;
Typed Hono.js routes, grouped by resource (routes/users.ts, routes/orders.ts...);
Vitest tests generated in mirror of the routes;
The OpenAPI 3.1 spec and a ready-to-use Swagger UI.
sections.outro: You can edit directly in the console, or download the Git repo as a zip / git push.

sections.heading: 4. Deploy
sections.intro: Three paths. Choose based on your comfort level:

items.label: ZeroAPI hosting
items.body: (Pro plan): one click, one subdomain *.zeroapi.app, and it's live.

items.label: Deploy with a partner
items.body: : connect your Railway, Render, Fly.io, or Vercel account. ZeroAPI generates the Dockerfile and associated manifest.

items.label: Git export
items.body: : take the repo, do whatever you like. No magic link back to ZeroAPI — you leave free.

sections.heading: 5. What's next?
sections.body: Read the guides for advanced use cases (payments, SSO, multi-tenant, signed webhooks), browse the API reference for endpoint-by-endpoint details, or check out our templates if you prefer to start from an existing base.

meta.description: Concrete patterns for ZeroAPI backends: authentication, Mobile Money, RBAC, webhooks, multi-tenant.

guides.title: Guides
guides.intro: Every guide starts from a real problem and ends with a backend that solves it. Commented code, screenshots, prompt ready to copy.

items.title: JWT + OAuth Google / GitHub
items.desc: Enable sign-in via external providers, manage rotating refresh tokens, and link multiple identities to a single account.

items.title: Two-factor authentication (TOTP)
items.desc: Enforce 2FA for admin roles, manage recovery codes and trusted sessions.

items.title: SSO SAML / OIDC for enterprise
items.desc: Connect Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace. Auto-provisioning and group mapping.

items.title: Integrate Wave, Orange Money, MTN MoMo
items.desc: Signed webhook, idempotent status, daily reconciliation. The generated code handles all three in a single flow.

items.title: Stripe for card payments
items.desc: Hosted checkout, verified Stripe webhooks, dispute and refund management.

items.title: Fine-grained RBAC by role and resource
items.desc: Define nested roles, restrict by field, and generate automatically tested policies.

items.title: Rate limiting by token and IP
items.desc: Configure limits per endpoint, handle bursts and exemptions for trusted partners.

items.title: Multi-tenant: isolating workspaces
items.desc: Shared schema or DB per tenant, context middleware, guardrails to prevent cross-tenant leaks.

items.title: Signed outgoing webhooks
items.desc: Notify third-party systems with exponential retry, HMAC signature, and delivery journal.

items.title: Scheduled tasks (cron) and queues
items.desc: Run recurring jobs, manage replays and the dead-letter queue.

meta.title: API Reference — ZeroAPI
meta.description: Complete reference for REST endpoints generated by ZeroAPI: auth, CRUD, filters, pagination, error codes.

api.title: API
api.subtitle: All responses are JSON, encoded in UTF-8, with a Content-Type: application/json header.
api.callout: The generated code includes a /openapi.json route and a Swagger UI at /docs. What follows is the common base; your specific schema is served by your deployed backend.
api.authNote: All protected routes expect a header:
api.rateLimitsBody: By default, 120 requests / minute per authenticated token, 60 / minute per unauthenticated IP. Three headers are returned on every response: RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset. Adjustable per endpoint in the generated code.

groups.intro: All authentication endpoints return a JWT access token and a rotating refresh token. Store the refresh token in an HTTP-only cookie.

eps.desc: Creates a new account with an email and password. Sends a verification email.

params.name: email
params.desc: Valid email, not already in use.

eps.desc: Authenticates an existing user. Returns an access token and sets a refresh cookie.
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access + refresh pair.
Revokes the current refresh token and clears the associated cookie.

groups.intro: For each entity declared in your prompt, ZeroAPI generates these five endpoints respecting the configured RBAC. Example here on the users resource.

eps.desc: Paginated list of users. Supports filters, sorting, and cursor pagination.

params.name: cursor
params.desc: Opaque cursor returned by the previous request.

eps.desc: Creates a new resource. Body validated by Zod according to the declared schema.
Retrieves a resource by its unique identifier.
Partial update. Absent fields are left unchanged.
Soft delete by default. Add `?hard=true` to delete permanently (admin only).

groups.intro: ZeroAPI generates two endpoints to manage files via signed URLs to an S3-compatible bucket (R2, Backblaze, AWS).

eps.desc: Requests a signed upload URL. Returns the URL and the final `key`.

params.name: contentType
params.desc: MIME type validated against a whitelist.

eps.desc: Confirms the upload after the client-side PUT. Creates the metadata row in the database.

errors.name: Bad Request
errors.desc: Zod validation failed — see the `details` array.

errors.name: Forbidden
errors.desc: Authenticated but without the required role.

errors.name: Not Found
errors.desc: Resource does not exist or is outside the current tenant.

errors.name: Unprocessable
errors.desc: Valid format but semantics refused (e.g. impossible state transition).

errors.name: Server Error
errors.desc: Internal error. Tracked and notified to the team.
